title: Getting around
can: Ask where things are, follow directions, and buy a return ticket.
doneText: You can now find what you need in a Spanish town, ask the way and follow the answer.

discover.intro: All six sentences are about where things are. See if you can spot when Spanish says hay and when it says está.

groups.label: With hay
lines: Is there a pharmacy around here?
Hay un bar en la esquina.
There's a bar on the corner.

groups.label: With está
lines: El bar está en la esquina.
The bar is on the corner.

discover.question: When does Spanish use hay, and when está?
options: Hay introduces something new (un, una, or no article). Está locates a specific thing you already know (el, la, my, a name).
Hay is for places, está is for people.
Hay is the past tense of está.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look at the little word in front of each place: una and un in blue, la and el in orange.
discover.reveal: Hay means "there is" or "there are" and introduces something new. Está (están for plurals) says where a specific thing is. Two hooks:

hooks.title: hay: there is, there are
rows: Is there a cash machine around here?
There are some very good bars.

hooks.title: está: where it is
rows: Mi hotel está en el centro.
My hotel is in the centre.
The toilets are at the back.

learn.title: Finding your way
learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: a + el = al and de + el = del: al final de la calle, al lado del hotel. With la nothing joins up: al lado de la estación.
Here coger means to take (a bus, a street, a train): coge la segunda a la derecha. In much of Latin America it is rude, so keep it for Spain.

blocks.title: Recto or derecha
blocks.note: Recto sounds like "right", but todo recto means straight on. Right is a la derecha.

blocks.text: Gira, sigue, cruza and coge are commands for tú. They look just like the él / ella form (gira = she turns), which makes them easy to remember. To a stranger you may hear the usted forms: gire, siga, cruce, coja.

phrases.en: Is there a pharmacy around here?

phrases.es: Un billete de ida y vuelta, por favor.

phrases.en: How do I get to the centre?

exercises.sub: (Is there a cash machine around here?)
exercises.why: Un cajero is any cash machine, something new: hay.
El museo is a specific place: está.

items.full: La farmacia está en la esquina.
items.why: La farmacia, a specific one: está.

items.full: Hay muchos bares en esta calle.
items.why: Introducing them: hay. Hay never changes for plurals.

items.full: Mi hotel está en el centro.
No hay metro en este pueblo.

items.why: La parada, a specific stop: está.

items.blank: ___ un supermercado al lado del hotel.
items.full: Hay un supermercado al lado del hotel.

items.why: A name is always specific: está.

exercises.say: Gira a la izquierda y sigue todo recto.
options: Turn left and keep going straight on.
Turn right and take the second street.
exercises.why: Izquierda is left, todo recto is straight on.

exercises.q: El cajero está al lado ___ hotel.
exercises.why: De + el always joins up: del.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.sentence: El museo hay en el centro.
exercises.fixed: El museo está en el centro.
exercises.why: El museo is specific, so está. Hay introduces something new: hay un museo en el centro.

exercises.q: Is there a bus stop around here?
answer: hay una parada de autobús por aquí
hay una parada de autobús cerca
exercises.why: Any bus stop, something new: ¿Hay una parada…?

exercises.prompt: Take the second street on the right.
exercises.answer: Coge la segunda calle a la derecha.
exercises.why: Coger = to take, in Spain. A la derecha = on the right.

exercises.q: Gira a la derecha ___ final de la calle.
exercises.why: A + el always joins up: al final.

exercises.prompt: You want to go to Toledo and come back the same day. Ask for…
options: un billete de ida y vuelta
exercises.why: Ida y vuelta is there and back. Ida alone is one way.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: Straight on is todo recto. Derecha means right.
Gira to a friend, gire to a stranger. Left is izquierda.

exercises.q: El hotel está ___ de la estación.

exercises.why: A specific place you've already mentioned: está. Lejos = far.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Give a friend directions from your hostel to a café: use at least two directions, then say where the café is.
write.starter: Gira a la…  Sigue…  El café está…
write.model: Gira a la derecha y sigue todo recto. Coge la segunda calle a la izquierda. El café está al lado de la farmacia, enfrente del parque.
checklist: Directions use gira, sigue or coge
The café is specific, so está
de + el becomes del, a + el becomes al

boss.title: Lost near Puerta del Sol
boss.persona: You are Marta, a friendly woman from Madrid near the Puerta del Sol. The learner is lost and asks you for directions. Give simple directions (todo recto, a la derecha, a la izquierda, al lado de, enfrente de) to places like the metro, a pharmacy, the Prado museum or a café. Use tú.

turns.en: Hi! Can I help you? Are you lost?
choices: Sí. ¿Dónde está el metro, por favor?
Sí. ¿Dónde hay el metro, por favor?
El metro is a specific place: ¿Dónde está…?
Sí. ¿Dónde es el metro, por favor?
Location uses estar: ¿Dónde está…?

turns.npc: Sigue todo recto y gira a la izquierda. Está enfrente de la farmacia.
turns.en: Go straight on and turn left. It's opposite the pharmacy.
choices: Todo recto, a la izquierda, enfrente de la farmacia. Gracias.
A la derecha, al lado de la farmacia. Gracias.
She said a la izquierda (left) and enfrente de (opposite).
Todo recto, a la derecha, enfrente de la farmacia. Gracias.
She said a la izquierda: left. Derecha is right.

turns.en: You're welcome. Do you need anything else?
choices: Sí, ¿hay un cajero por aquí?
Sí, ¿está un cajero por aquí?
Any cash machine is something new: ¿Hay un cajero…?
Sí, ¿dónde hay el cajero?
With el (a specific one), use está. For any cash machine: ¿Hay un cajero…?

turns.npc: Sí, hay uno al lado del banco, en la esquina.
turns.en: Yes, there's one next to the bank, on the corner.
choices: ¿Al lado del banco? Perfecto, muchas gracias.
¿Al lado de el banco? Perfecto, muchas gracias.
De + el always joins up: del banco.
¿Lejos del banco? Perfecto, muchas gracias.
She said al lado (next to), not lejos (far).

boss.closingEn: You're welcome! Have a good day!
boss.chatOpeningEn: And where are you going afterwards? To the Prado?
